articles.title: Closure Order Issued for Phantom The Lounge Due to Carbon Monoxide Risks
articles.excerpt: Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road has been closed by Rochdale Council due to excessive carbon monoxide levels posing a risk to customers and staff.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 31 July 2026 at 12:00. 2 source updates have been combined into this article.

Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road has been closed by Rochdale Council due to excessive carbon monoxide levels posing a risk to customers and staff.

Latest update

A shisha lounge on Maclure Road has been handed a closure order following the discovery of excessive levels of carbon monoxide (CO) on site. The order for Phantom The Lounge was granted at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on 24 July 2026, based on evidence provided by environmental health officers from Rochdale Borough Council, supported by Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) and Greater Manchester Police (GMP).

Routine inspections revealed that the lounge had been operating illegally, allowing smoking in a substantially enclosed area, which contravenes the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006. In addition to the illegal smoking, officers found hazardous practices in the kitchen, including the use of an electric fan to smoulder hot coals in an unventilated area, leading to CO levels exceeding 100 parts per million (PPM).

On two occasions, GMFRS instructed customers and staff to leave the premises for their safety. Despite the council's attempts to work with the owners to rectify the issues, the business continued to operate without making necessary changes, prompting the council's environmental health service to seek a court closure as a last resort.

Councillor Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader and portfolio holder for Climate Change and Environment, stated that the high levels of CO posed a significant risk to health. She commended the efforts of environmental health officers and partners for their timely intervention, which prevented further danger to the public.

Earlier developments

A shisha lounge in Rochdale has been closed after environmental health officers discovered excessive levels of carbon monoxide on the premises. Phantom The Lounge, located on Maclure Road, was ordered to shut down by Rochdale Council's environmental health service following a court order granted at Manchester Magistrates' Court on July 24.

The closure came after a routine inspection revealed that the lounge had been illegally operating with smoking occurring in a substantially enclosed area, violating the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006. In addition to this, hazardous practices in the kitchen were identified, which exposed both customers and workers to carbon monoxide levels exceeding 100 parts per million (PPM).

Rochdale Council stated that an electric fan was used to smoulder coals in an unventilated area, leading to dangerous conditions. On two occasions, fire officers had to instruct customers and staff to leave the site for their safety. The council had previously offered the owners an opportunity to rectify the issues, but they refused to cooperate, prompting the court action as a last resort.

Councillor Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader and portfolio holder for Climate Change and Environment, emphasised the risks posed by high levels of carbon monoxide, stating that the health of customers and staff was at stake. She noted the importance of health regulations in ensuring safe business operations and indicated that action would be taken against those who fail to comply. Carbon monoxide is a colourless and odourless gas that can cause serious health issues, including loss of consciousness and death.

articles.title: Rochdale Mental Health Worker Recognised for Saving Person from Canal
articles.excerpt: A mental health worker from Rochdale has received recognition from the council for his actions in saving a person from a canal, demonstrating bravery and compassion.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale mental health worker has been recognised for his actions after he saved a person from a canal. Marcus Urey received 'heroic recognition' from Rochdale Borough Council for his bravery and compassion in the incident.

Mr Urey, who works at Stansfield Place, a rehabilitation centre for men with serious mental illnesses, acted quickly to assist the person while off duty. The Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust commended his actions, stating he showed bravery in a difficult situation.

At a ceremony at the town hall, Mr Urey was presented with a certificate by mayor Faisal Rana and mayoress Iram Faisal. The trust highlighted that care and compassion extend beyond work hours, praising Mr Urey for ensuring the person received the necessary support after the incident.

In a statement, Mr Urey expressed gratitude for being in the right place at the right time, stating, 'I did what I hope anyone would do to help someone in need.' He added that he was humbled by the recognition from his colleagues. The trust emphasised that Mr Urey's actions exemplified the values of care and compassion that are central to their work. His quick response not only saved a life but also ensured that the person received the support they needed afterwards.

articles.title: New Structured Medication Review Service Launched in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Bespoke Clinical Services has launched a new Structured Medication Review Service in Rochdale. This initiative aims to enhance patient care by providing comprehensive medication reviews. The service is designed to help patients manage their medications more effectively, ensuring they receive the right treatment for their health conditions.
articles.content_html:
Bespoke Clinical Services has launched a new Structured Medication Review Service in Rochdale. This initiative aims to enhance patient care by providing comprehensive medication reviews.

The service is designed to help patients manage their medications more effectively, ensuring they receive the right treatment for their health conditions.

Healthcare professionals will conduct detailed assessments of patients' medication regimens, identifying any potential issues and making necessary adjustments.

This new service is expected to improve health outcomes for residents in Rochdale, promoting better management of chronic conditions and overall well-being.
